title: USA Chicken Feet Dog Chews: Remy's Test Notes
description: Remy tested USA Chicken Feet dog chews. A natural single-ingredient chew that lasts 20 to 25 minutes, has low odor, and is good for dental health. Great for a quicker chew session.
card_summary: Remy was curious at first, now loves them. 20 to 25 minutes per chew, low smell, good for teeth. A versatile option when you want something quicker than a bully stick.

verdict_title: Remy approved, a solid quick chew
verdict_text: Clean, low-odor, single-ingredient chews that Remy is now fully into. They are shorter sessions than a bully stick, which makes them a versatile option depending on what you need.

surfaces.name: First reaction
surfaces.note: Remy was curious and a little unsure at first. After a couple of tries, he was fully into them. Worth sticking with if your dog takes a minute to warm up.

surfaces.name: Chew time
surfaces.note: About 20 to 25 minutes per foot. Not as long as a bully stick, but enough to give them something to work on.

surfaces.name: Odor check
surfaces.note: Low smell. One of the better options if you are sensitive to chew odor in the house.

surfaces.name: Teeth and gums
surfaces.note: Chicken feet are naturally high in glucosamine and the texture works against tartar. Not a replacement for brushing, but a useful side benefit.

what_we_tested:
We gave Remy the USA Chicken Feet chews across a few sessions. He was not immediately sure what to do with them the first time, which is pretty normal for a new texture or shape. After a couple of tries he was clearly into them.

We use these when we want something quicker than a bully stick, or when we want to give Remy something to do without committing to a full long-chew session.
what_worked:
The smell is genuinely low compared to most chews. That alone makes these easier to use around the house.

They last Remy about **20 to 25 minutes**, which makes them good for situations where you want to keep him occupied for a bit without a full bully-stick session. Versatile in that way — works as enrichment, a quick reward, or something to wind him down.

Clean ingredient list. The listing says 100% natural, water-washed only, single ingredient. No additives to worry about.

Chicken feet are naturally high in glucosamine and cartilage, and the texture does some work on teeth and gums as your dog chews through them.
what_didnt_work:
Remy needed a couple of tries to get comfortable with them. If your dog is picky about new textures or shapes, give it more than one session before writing them off.

The 2.5-pound value pack is about 115 feet, which is a lot. Make sure you have storage sorted before ordering.
remys_take: Took him a minute to get there, but now he grabs one without hesitation. These have become a regular rotation chew when we want something quicker.
worth_buying: Yes. If you want a low-odor, short-session chew with a clean ingredient list and a natural dental benefit, chicken feet are a good pick. The value pack makes the price work out well per chew.

faqs.question: How long does a chicken foot chew last a dog?
faqs.answer: Remy gets about 20 to 25 minutes out of one. It varies by dog size and chew style, but they are not a long-session chew.

faqs.question: Do chicken feet dog chews smell?
faqs.answer: The smell is low. These are one of the more odor-friendly chew options we have tested.

faqs.question: Are chicken feet good for dogs' teeth?
faqs.answer: The natural texture and cartilage in chicken feet can help with tartar, and they are high in glucosamine. They are not a replacement for actual dental care, but it is a useful side benefit.

faqs.question: What are these chicken feet made from?
faqs.answer: The listing says 100% natural chicken feet, water-washed only, single ingredient. No additives or preservatives listed.

faqs.question: What if my dog is not interested right away?
faqs.answer: Remy was curious but unsure at first. After a couple of sessions he was fully into them. Give it a few tries before deciding if your dog does not go for it immediately.
